subject: Calypso v2 onboarding — tokenization mismatch and temporary pin request
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Calypso v2 onboarding — tokenization mismatch and temporary pin request

Team,

We ran the initial ingest of Calypso-8B-v2 artifacts from Atlas this morning and hit a tokenization mismatch during staging evals. The model uses a slightly different BPE vocabulary (3K added tokens) and the tokenizer id differs from what our serving runtime expects. That divergence is causing truncated prompts in a subset of our tests.

Ask: I'd like to request a short-term pin of Calypso-8B-v1 (existing variant) for up to 7 days while infra and model teams remediate. During that window we should:
- Confirm tokenization delta and produce deterministic conversion or mapping.
- Run a 24h canary on dedicated (10% traffic) to validate metrics.
- Prepare rollback / fallback mapping if inference errors surface.

Attachments: calypso-v2-diff-report.pdf (scanner output from embed/inference tests)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Calypso-Onboard

Laid out below are specific asks by owner — please reply with timing/caveats.

Laura
Laura Bennett
PM, Model Ops
Redwood Inference
From: dev.patel@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calypso v2 onboarding — tokenization mismatch and temporary pin request

Quick technical recap from infra: the tokenizer id mismatch is the root cause — Calypso-v2 embeds a new vocab block and registers a different tokenizer signature. Our runtime expects the previous tokenizer artifacts; without conversion the model will encode inputs differently and break prompt lengths.

Options I see:
1) Conversion pipeline: add a migration step that maps v2 vocab indices to our canonical ids + rebuild tokenizer artifacts. Estimated 3–5 business days (including validation).
2) Runtime shim: implement a fallback tokenizer mapping layer that remaps input ids at decode time for affected routes. Estimated 2–3 business days but adds runtime overhead.
3) Quick soft-pin: keep v1 serving for public traffic and route invited customers or internal tests to v2. This requires an orchestration pin and a temporary routing rule.

I'll attach the initial patch for the conversion (tokenizer-patch.patch) and a short test harness. If we go conversion-first I recommend freezing rollout until we finish a token-level validation sweep.

Attachments: tokenizer-patch.patch
Gist: https://gist.github.com/devpatel/calypso-tokenizer-diff

- Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calypso v2 onboarding — tokenization mismatch and temporary pin request

Thanks — this is helpful context. From a release/ops standpoint I need the following before I can approve any pin or canary:
- Risk assessment (SLO/latency delta + failure modes)
- Canary runbook (metrics, thresholds, rollback triggers)
- Cost delta for keeping v1 pinned (GPU hours estimate)
- Targeted routes for the canary (which customers / API keys)

If we pin v1 I propose a strict 7-day window with daily checkpoints. Marissa can own the rollout and rollback choreography; Dev, can you confirm the expected latency hit for the runtime shim option? Vivek, any constraints from product roadmap (icons/feature flags) here?

I can prep a canary runbook draft (canary-runbook.md) and a short customer notification template if needed.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Release Manager
From: Clare Jackson <clare.jackson@atlas.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calypso v2 onboarding — tokenization mismatch and temporary pin request

Laura / team,

Thanks for the heads up. We shipped the model artifact with the expanded vocab intentionally to support domain tokens for Atlas customers — the change was documented in our release notes but I apologize if it didn't surface in the artifact manifest you read.

S3 path: s3://atlas-artifacts/calypso/v2/calypso-8b-v2.tar.gz
SHA256: 9b2f4f7a8c0f2b3e4d5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7
Planned maintenance window: Mar 10–12 for our integration tests. We can hold off the public switch until you validate.

Happy to coordinate — if you want a small shadow test harness pointing at our tokens we can stand that up by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Clare
Clare Jackson
Partner Engineering, Atlas AI
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Clare Jackson <clare.jackson@atlas.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calypso v2 onboarding — tokenization mismatch and temporary pin request

Decision and next steps: thank you all for fast responses. I'm approving a temporary pin of Calypso-8B-v1 for a maximum of 7 days to buy the team time for a proper fix. Conditions:
1) Dev to scope conversion vs shim by end of day tomorrow and recommend the lowest-risk path.
2) Marissa to run the 10% dedicated canary with the runbook and thresholds; daily checkpoints at 10:00 PST.
3) Laura to own comms with Atlas and any customers affected; Clare, please share the shadow harness if you can.
4) If a conversion commit is not ready within 5 business days, escalate to me and we'll decide whether to extend the pin.

Please update JIRA-INF-9821 with the selected approach and drop the canary artifacts into the Drive folder. I'll sign off on the pin in the console once Marissa confirms the runbook and Dev posts perf numbers.

Jonas Weber
Director, Product
Redwood Inference
